solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sad time to return to Havana, say

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for a Havana is read backwards

parts.note: a Havana is an example of a cigar, signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone feels sad that it is time to go back to Cuba's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Havana' looks like the city, but 'say' marks it as an example: a Havana cigar. 'to return' turns CIGAR into RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is deeply sorrowful, a close synonym of sad.

clue.text: Involuntary response of judge to law

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a game
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A judge reacts automatically to the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an automatic bodily reaction made without conscious thought.

clue.text: Sporting type, old, turning up to shoot bird on river

indicators.note: to shoot means to pass right through, so the reversed word goes inside

parts.note: a goose is a bird

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old sportsman turns up to shoot a goose on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses OLD to DLO, which shoots through GOOSE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts defeat graciously is a sporting type.

clue.text: Dormant recording of "Christopher … down with Alice"?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: the dormant stage of an insect

indicators.note: a recording of words reproduces their sound, so the answer is spoken like them

parts.note: Christopher cut down gives Chris, said with Alice

explanation.surface: Like a song title, a quiet recording of Christopher Robin going down with Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis echoes the Milne song 'They're changing guard at Buckingham Palace — Christopher Robin went down with Alice'; 'down' also shortens Christopher to Chris.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is the resting pupa of a butterfly, a dormant phase before emergence.

clue.text: Climactic finale of entertainment for county

parts.note: a show is a piece of entertainment
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The big closing number of a show put on for a county audience.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is the decisive final confrontation that a story builds towards, its climax.

clue.text: What's poisonous about Conservative unbeliever

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the infected word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: septic means infected, poisonous

explanation.surface: Something toxic surrounds a doubting Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts accepted beliefs, a synonym of unbeliever.

clue.text: Beast with notoriety cut short by relief agency

parts.note: an ox is a beast

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: fame is notoriety, being widely known

explanation.surface: A notorious animal is curtailed by an aid charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a well-known British charity that delivers relief and development aid worldwide.

clue.text: Christmas coming? Gold furnishings required

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, shortened to Dec
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: With Christmas coming, gold furnishings are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming' and 'required' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the furnishing and decoration of a room.

clue.text: Seek to win over somewhat reduced musicians

parts.note: to woo is to seek to win someone over

indicators.note: somewhat signals only part of the word for reduced is used

parts.note: dwindled means reduced

explanation.surface: Trying to win over a shrinking band.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodwind section of an orchestra is a group of players of flutes, oboes and the like.

clue.text: 100 in 4s, in Old English obviously

indicators.note: the second in puts all of that within the abbreviation for the old language
in places the numeral's letter inside the spelt-out number

parts.note: 4s spelt out in words is fours
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A dry-looking sum about a hundred in fours, set in the language of Beowulf, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: '4s' must be spelt out in words; each 'in' signals its own nesting, the numeral inside the number, then that inside the old language.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday adverbial meaning naturally or evidently, a synonym of obviously.

clue.text: Performance goes in for, say, 4 of 100

indicators.note: goes in tells us the word for a performance enters the word for

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A stage act gets a turn standing in for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 9-across's numbers: 4 divides 100 exactly, so it is an example of the answer, flagged by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor of a number divides it exactly; 4 goes into 100 twenty-five times, so it is one example.

clue.text: The guy will like Greece

parts.note: the guy will contracts to he'll, a male pronoun plus will
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

explanation.surface: A man says he will be fond of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like a verb of fondness but stands for AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellas is the Greek name for Greece, used in English for the ancient and modern country.

clue.text: Schoolboy has grave quarrel with Pole

parts.note: a tomb is a grave
a row is a quarrel
N, north, is one of the two poles

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is caught up in a graveside argument with a Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a magnetic or geographic pole, N. Thomas Hughes's novel Tom Brown's Schooldays is set at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Tom Brown's Schooldays is the best-known schoolboy in English fiction.

clue.text: Live school produced cookbook

definitions.note: describes a person: one who produced a cookbook

parts.note: to be is to live, exist
Eton is a famous English school

explanation.surface: A school with boarders put out a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861) is Britain's classic cookbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella Beeton wrote the most famous Victorian household cookery book.

clue.text: Holiday to ensure square meals, rectangles if desired

indicators.note: desired suggests the shapes can be made however one wishes, so the letters are reworked into any order

explanation.surface: A holiday where you get proper meals, cut into rectangles if you like.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'square meals' could be served as rectangles on request; 'desired' rearranges RECTANGLES IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-catering holiday gives you a kitchen so you cook your own food, guaranteeing meals as you want them.

clue.text: Brains trust, inadequate, two kings are about to give hiding to

parts.note: thin means inadequate, as in a thin excuse

indicators.note: are about means the two letters surround the beating word

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, twice
to tan is to give a hiding, a beating

explanation.surface: Weak experts: two kings are about to beat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of experts consulted for ideas, as in the old radio Brains Trust panel.

clue.text: Expression of contempt for cane?

definitions.meaning: a rude noise made by blowing through the lips
the long stem of a soft-fruit bush is a cane

explanation.walkthrough: 'cane' looks like a punishment stick but is a fruit plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The rude noise is called blowing one, and the fruit grows on canes.

clue.text: China tea attractive?

parts.note: char is slang for tea
Ming is a Chinese dynasty famous for porcelain

explanation.surface: Is Chinese tea attractive?
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the opposite order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming means pleasing and delightful, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Literary genre gives spirits to Conservatives

parts.note: shorts are measures of spirits such as whisky or gin, served as small drinks
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A literary type pours drinks for a crowd of Tory politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'short' is a small measure of spirits, as opposed to a long drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief prose fiction is a recognised category of literature, distinct from the novel.

clue.text: See 13
Twitching in stone must be a sort of illusion

indicators.note: in means the twitch goes inside the gemstone

parts.note: an opal is a precious stone
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A twitch inside a stone must be a trick of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a well-known kind of illusion, so the adjective classifies it.

clue.text: Peace's shattered — flee!

indicators.note: shattered means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peace is broken, run away!
explanation.walkthrough: The 's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get away, a synonym of flee.

clue.text: Expecting little prince to be on the throne

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for prince, so 'little' signals the short form
regnant means reigning, being on the throne

explanation.surface: A young prince expects to succeed to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like awaiting the crown but means carrying a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is the everyday euphemism for carrying a child.

clue.text: Entrances philanthropist

definitions.meaning: Bill ..., the Microsoft founder known for charitable giving

explanation.definitionFit: Gates are entrances, and Bill Gates is a famous philanthropist.

clue.text: Markswoman involved in tyrannies

indicators.note: involved in means contained within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter caught up in oppressions.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Oakley was a celebrated American sharpshooter.

clue.text: Terminate using bludgeon, Spooner style

indicators.note: Spooner style asks us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: by means using, as in by hand
a cosh is a short heavy club

explanation.surface: An instruction to end something with a blunt instrument, said in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: BY COSH swapped by sound gives 'ki bosh', the C and K sounding alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is to stop it dead; the word is also used as a verb meaning end.

clue.text: Author's including Eeyore with new head in new town

indicators.note: including shows the author's name holding another word inside it

parts.note: A. A. Milne wrote the Pooh stories; with the 's this gives the letters MILNES

indicators.note: with new head means the first letter of the animal is replaced by another

parts.note: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in the Pooh stories

explanation.surface: An author, with a donkey character redesigned, is set in a planned town.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's town tempts John Milton as the author, but it is Eeyore's creator; the donkey's replacement first letter is T, which the clue leaves unstated.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes in Buckinghamshire is the best-known of the post-war planned settlements designated as new towns in England.

clue.text: Companion to flier who's sitting down?

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
an airman is someone who flies

explanation.surface: A companion for a pilot is sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal letters for a Companion of Honour. The definition is playful: a chair person is literally one sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a meeting is literally the one in the chair, so a jokey description of the presiding figure.

clue.text: China gives spur to the underground

parts.note: to egg someone on is to spur them, so eggs means gives a spur
hell is traditionally placed beneath the earth

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain urges someone towards the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the underground' looks like the railway but is the underworld, HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is a very thin, delicate porcelain.

clue.text: See 26
